title: CMOSP18 FD-SOI Technology Based MCU Achieving High Performance of 1.2GHz Using High Speed, Optimized Leakage & High Density Tightly Coupled Memory (TCM)
problem: Microcontroller units (MCUs) require both high performance (>1GHz) and low-leakage operation. Tightly coupled memories (TCM) are critical for processor performance but consume significant power and area. Optimizing TCM for both speed and leakage is challenging without degrading performance.
motivation: Physically embedded TCM close to processor cores dictates overall system performance. Dual-optimization for leakage (for far TCM) and speed (for near TCM) enables better power efficiency without compromising performance. High-density bitcells reduce RC delays, improving both speed and area.
method: Two TCM variants in CMOSP18 FD-SOI technology: (1) performance-optimized instances for TCM placed closer to core (standard timing); (2) leakage-optimized instances for far TCM placement (reduced VDD, optimized gates). Both use high-density bitcells to reduce area and RC delay.
key_novelty: Dual-variant TCM optimization strategy targeting spatial proximity within same core: performance optimization for near-core TCM, leakage optimization for distant TCM, using high-density bitcell design.
contributions: 1.2 GHz MCU clock frequency in CMOSP18 FD-SOI technology
16% reduction in access + setup time vs. competitor TCM design
33% reduction in leakage power vs. competitor design
17% reduction in area vs. competitor design
High-density bitcell implementation for improved speed and area
limitations: Abstract only; no detailed bitcell design or optimization methodology provided; specific leakage optimization techniques not disclosed; performance degradation from leakage optimization not quantified; area breakdown (bitcell vs. periphery) not specified; PVT robustness not analyzed; generalization to other technologies not discussed; comparison limited to single unnamed competitor.
